## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c5d1fddde28602e282dbf7680bbdb5b7dec79c9f`
Local-runs: probe — one `check-governed-merges.mjs --test scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs` path-predicate call, run to say whether the must-fix's fix file is governed; it was not needed (the register rows answer it by reading) and nothing in this record rests on its output. Nothing built, no self-test or gate re-run, no checkout.
Scope: none (`reviewFace` hits: ungoverned); judged as the contract files: scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs + none (the diff holds those two files only)

Read: card #33620 body and its 3 comments (triage 6888758949, claim 6893186109, os-dev-report 6893465272); PR #33804 body and file list (2 files, +146 / -26); the net diff of the head against its merge base `b76df9a6980` (one commit; main is one commit ahead, #33725, which touches neither file); the check-runs on the head. Read, not reviewed: `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs`, `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, `scripts/git-env.mjs`, `.github/workflows/lint.yml` at the head.

Check-runs on the head when this record was written: `Lint · repo & tooling gates` FAILURE (see M1). Still running: `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Test Core (1/8)`. Green: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Test Core (2/8)`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Test UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Queue guard `enumerateRows`, both legs (`pull_request` net row, `merge_group` per-commit row): `diff-tree ... --name-only -z`, split on NUL, empty fields dropped. Right. `--name-only -z` has no status field and `--no-renames` is kept, so there is no two-path record to mis-split.
- `check-governed-merges.mjs` `deriveBranchPaths`: `diff -z --name-only --no-renames`, split on NUL. Right. `tryGit` still trims the whole output; a NUL is not whitespace, so only leading whitespace of the first path can be lost, and that can only turn an ungoverned name into a governed one, never the reverse.
- `commitChanges`: `diff-tree --numstat -z --no-renames`, one `added TAB deleted TAB path` record per NUL, the path group widened to cross a newline. Right: `--no-renames` rules out the three-field rename form of `--numstat -z`, and a binary row (`- TAB -`) still matches.
- `readWorkflowDiff` `listAt`: `ls-tree -r -z --name-only`, split on NUL, no per-name trim. Right.
- Every path read in the two files that feeds a governed or tier decision was found. Greps of the head for `diff-tree`, `diff`, `ls-tree`, `ls-files`, `log`, `show`, `status`, `--name-only`, `--name-status`, `--numstat`, `--raw`, `--porcelain` leave, outside the self-tests: the three already `-z` reads (`catalogFilesOf` `--raw -z`, the carried-head `diff -z --name-only`, `armReadsNotMeasured` `ls-tree -z`); two SIZE reads that sum counts only; `pullCatalogReading` `ls-tree SHA -- PATH`, which parses the mode only; and `log` reads that carry no path. No reader compares a quoted path string any more.
- Accept-set moves, each judged:
  - A governed path git quotes: UNGOVERNED before, governed now, in the queue leg, `--branch` and the sweep. Right, the card's defect.
  - A workflow whose name git quotes, in the queue leg and `--branch`: not seen before, now governed and classified (S or H by content). Stricter. Right.
  - The same workflow under `--pr` and the fleet-write executor (paths from the API, raw): Tier H before by "absent at both commits", now classified, so a timeout-only edit reads Tier S. This is one H to S move; judged in ③, correct reading.
  - The inventory ("already in use" at the merge base) now includes workflows whose names git quotes; before they were dropped by the prefix filter. An action only such a workflow uses now vouches for another workflow's `uses:`, a second narrow H to S direction the PR body does not name. Correct under the ruling's words ("a `uses:` no workflow uses at the base"); see N1.
  - Every ASCII path reads the same bytes on all five reads.
- Public surface: none. No package, no schema, no exported signature changed; `renderDerivation` prints `git diff -z --name-only --no-renames`, the command that ran.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: `scripts/pm/**` publishes nothing, no package is touched. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body match the claim comment 6893186109 and the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Developer flag, the quoted-name workflow reading Tier S: NOT a fail-open. The workflows split (ruling record 6722205630, header section "The workflows row's split") makes a file H by PATH (the six pinned files, all ASCII, unchanged) or H by DIFF (C2 triggers), and S otherwise. The file name's encoding is no trigger. The earlier Tier H under `--pr` was a failed measurement with a false reason, and in the queue leg the same file was not governed at all, which is the larger hole this PR closes. Taken literally, the dispatch sentence "nothing that reads Tier H today may read Tier S" is breached on this one reading; the seat should accept it as a named deviation (the PR body's Acceptance notes state it), not treat it as a regression.
- `open_questions`: empty in the report. Nothing to answer.
- Out-of-file, `dispatch-gates.mjs` `changedPathsFromGit`: confirmed at the head (`diff --name-only --no-renames` twice and `ls-files --others`, no `-z`, each line trimmed). A `skills/**` path git quotes misses the `--tier` path mandate, so a dev can be dispatched below the mandated tier. The landing gates (queue guard, `--pr`) now catch the path, so this is a weaker-than-rule dispatch gate, not a landing hole. It needs its own card (tooling, p2 by the same reasoning as this card); the report lists it "noted, not filed", so the card is owed by the seat.
- Out-of-file, the `tryGit` leading-space note: agreed, no governed match can be lost. No card needed.
- New, for the seat: `dispatch-gates --commands` derived 35 gates on this diff and did not derive `pnpm check:pm-fleet-write-execute`, although `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs` imports `readWorkflowDiff` from a changed file and its self-test fakes that function's git argv. The report's "35 derived, 35 exit 0" is true and the head is still red (M1). The derivation gap deserves a card of its own.

### ④ Design judgment

- **M1, must-fix.** The head turns `Lint · repo & tooling gates` red. Step `Fleet-write executor self-test` (`pnpm check:pm-fleet-write-execute`) fails 2 of 415 cases: `tier-s-workflow-pull-requests-no-one` and `h-reading-workflow-pull-requests`, both with `git could not read the workflow files (fatal: not a tree object: --name-only)`. Cause: the `ls-tree` fake in `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs` (head lines 2993 to 2997) reads the revision at `argv[3]`, the directories from `argv.slice(5)`, and joins names with a newline; `readWorkflowDiff` now sends `-z` at index 2 and splits on NUL. The diff moved the same fake in both of its own files (index 3 to 4, 5 to 6, NUL join) and missed this third copy. Production fleet-write is not broken: `workflowReadingFor` hands real git to `readWorkflowDiff`. The fix is the same three-line move in that fake; the file is outside the claim's file surface (ungoverned, no register row), so the dev names the breach in the report. A delta review of the fix is owed.
- The four production reads agree with the card's item 1, sentence by sentence, and with the jsdoc the diff adds to `enumerateRows`, `commitChanges` and `readWorkflowDiff`.
- Card item 2 holds: real-git rows through `gitFreeEnv()` with a CJK name and a newline name under `skills/`, each with a CONTROL row proving the plain read quotes it, on both guard legs, `--branch`, the sweep and the workflow split. The PR body's ablation table was not re-run (read-only).
- Tried to break it: a name that is not valid UTF-8 decodes with replacement characters under `encoding: 'utf8'`; the ASCII governed prefix still matches, and a later `show SHA:PATH` fails into an unmeasured reading, Tier H. Fails closed. A path holding a TAB is kept whole by the greedy last group of the numstat pattern. A rename is two paths on every list read (`--no-renames` kept everywhere a path is listed).
- **N1, nit.** The PR body's Acceptance notes say a tier "can move one way only" plus the one workflow reading; the inventory widening in ① is a second reading that can move H to S and is not named. Prose face only.
- **N2, nit.** The CONTROL rows rely on git's default `core.quotePath`; `gitFreeEnv()` strips `GIT_*` variables but not a user or system gitconfig, so a machine with `core.quotePath=false` reads the CJK and `café` names raw and the CONTROL rows go red. It fails red, never falsely green. A `-c core.quotePath=true` on the control read would pin it; follow-up or accepted deviation.

- The fix is the move the prior record asked for and nothing else: the `ls-tree` fake in the executor self-test reads the revision at `argv[4]`, the directories from `argv.slice(6)`, and joins names with NUL. Ablation: with the `c5d1fddd` copy of the file restored on disk it is red again, exit 1, 2 of 415, exactly `tier-s-workflow-pull-requests-no-one` and `h-reading-workflow-pull-requests`, the two cases the prior record named; restored from the head, the worktree reads clean. `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --self-test`: 530 cases, exit 0.
- No other stale copy: a grep of `scripts/` for `ls-tree` fakes and for importers of `readWorkflowDiff`, `enumerateRows`, `commitChanges` and `deriveBranchPaths` finds the three PR files only. The remaining `ls-tree` users (`check-prior-rulings.mjs`, `ci/snapshot-next.mjs`, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `release-pending-publish.mjs`) do not reach the changed readers.
- Production is untouched by the delta: all nine changed lines sit inside `selfTest()`. No accept-set move.
- Card #33620, item by item, at this head: every path read that feeds a governed match in the queue guard and in `check-governed-merges.mjs` reads `-z` and splits on NUL (judged in the prior record, files unchanged since); the real-git rows with a non-ASCII and a newline name are in both self-tests.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `skip-changeset` is right, `scripts/pm/**` publishes nothing. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body match the three-file diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Surface breach, named: `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs` is outside the claim's file surface. The PR body names it under "Surface breach, named", with the reason (the stale fake, the prior record's M1) and its bound (test code only). `check-governed-merges.mjs --test` on the three paths reads 0 of 3 governed, so the breach adds no governed path and no approver. Accepted as a named deviation.
- The two H-to-S readings are both named in the PR body's Acceptance notes as accepted deviations, citing the prior record: (1) a modified workflow whose name git quotes is now classified like any other workflow edit; (2) such a workflow on the merge base now joins the "already in use" inventory. The prior record judged both correct under the workflows split of ruling record 6722205630; nothing in the delta changes that reading. This closes that record's N1 (prose face).
- N2 of the prior record (nit) stands as written: the CONTROL rows rely on git's default `core.quotePath`; it reads red, never falsely green, on a machine that sets it false. Accepted deviation or a follow-up card, the seat's choice; no effect on correctness or the contract.
- Still owed by the seat, from the prior record and not part of this PR: a card for `dispatch-gates.mjs` `changedPathsFromGit` (no `-z`), and one for the `--commands` derivation that did not name `check:pm-fleet-write-execute` for a diff that changed a function the executor self-test fakes. The PR body now reports 42 derived gates on the three-file diff, that gate among them.
- Check-runs on the head when this record was written: `Lint · repo & tooling gates` green (its step `Fleet-write executor self-test`, red on the prior head, passed). Green: `Auto Label`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · CI,  release & engine gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Test Core (2/8)`, `Test UI`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `filter`.
